question: What was InterGlobe Aviation's consolidated revenue from operations in FY24 and how much did it grow?
reference: Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs. 689,043.42 million in FY 2024, up from Rs. 544,464.53 million in FY 2023, a growth of about 26.6%.

question: What net profit did IndiGo report for FY24 compared with FY23?
reference: IndiGo reported a consolidated net profit of Rs. 81,724.68 million in FY 2024 against a net loss of Rs. 3,057.89 million in FY 2023.

question: How many passengers did IndiGo carry in FY24?
reference: IndiGo carried 106.42 million passengers in FY 2024, its first year above 100 million, a 24% increase over 85.59 million in FY 2023.

question: What was IndiGo's passenger load factor in FY24?
reference: The passenger load factor rose from 82.1% in FY 2023 to 85.9% in FY 2024.

question: How many Airbus A321neo aircraft were in IndiGo's fleet as of March 31, 2024?
reference: As of March 31, 2024 the fleet included 94 Airbus A321neo aircraft (alongside 192 A320neo, 20 A320ceo, 45 ATR, 3 A321 freighters and damp-leased B777 and A320 aircraft).

question: Did IndiGo's board recommend a dividend for FY24?
reference: No. Based on performance, cash flow and losses carried forward from previous years, the Board did not recommend any dividend on equity shares for FY 2024.

question: What was IndiGo's cost per available seat kilometre (CASK) in FY24 and why did it change?
reference: CASK decreased by 9.3% from Rs. 4.83 in FY 2023 to Rs. 4.38 in FY 2024, primarily driven by lower fuel cost and lower foreign exchange losses.

question: How did IndiGo's RASK change in FY24?
reference: RASK increased by 3.2% from Rs. 4.80 in FY 2023 to Rs. 4.96 in FY 2024, driven by higher yields and passenger load.

question: How much did IndiGo spend on aircraft fuel in FY24 and how did it compare with capacity growth?
reference: Aircraft fuel expenses rose only 1.1%, from Rs. 236,460.17 million to Rs. 239,045.78 million, against a 21.8% increase in capacity, mainly because ATF prices fell.

question: What was IndiGo's total cash position at the end of FY24?
reference: Total cash rose 48.3% to Rs. 347,375.29 million as of March 31, 2024: free cash of Rs. 208,229.91 million and restricted cash of Rs. 139,145.38 million.

question: Who are the statutory auditors of InterGlobe Aviation?
reference: M/s S.R. Batliboi & Co. LLP, Chartered Accountants, appointed at the 16th AGM on August 27, 2019.

question: How many permanent employees did IndiGo have at the end of FY24?
reference: The Company had 36,860 permanent employees on its rolls as on March 31, 2024.

question: What were IndiGo's Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions in FY24?
reference: Total Scope 1 emissions were 8,414,458.31 tonnes of CO2 equivalent in FY 2024, up from 6,789,520.00 in FY 2023.

question: How much did IndiGo spend on CSR in FY24?
reference: IndiGo spent Rs. 19,811,186 on CSR in FY 2024 although its statutory obligation (two percent of average net profit) was nil, so the whole amount was in excess of the requirement.

question: What were IndiGo's on-time performance and peak daily flights in FY24?
reference: On-time performance was 81.3% on DGCA metros, and peak operations reached 2,016 daily flights, 11% more than the 1,815 peak in FY 2023.

question: How many aircraft did IndiGo have on order according to its FY24 annual report?
reference: IndiGo had 985 aircraft on order, securing deliveries until the middle of the next decade, with an aim to become a 600+ aircraft carrier by 2030.

question: What did IndiGo account for in FY24 regarding aircraft grounded due to engine unavailability?
reference: IndiGo recorded an accrual for compensation from the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) for the ongoing Aircraft on Ground (AOG) situation caused by unavailability of engines, under Ind AS 115 and the existing contract, while a customised compensation plan was still being negotiated.

question: What was IndiGo's revenue from operations in FY25?
reference: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR 808,029 million in FY 2025 versus INR 689,043 million in FY 2024, growth of about 17.3%.

question: How did IndiGo's net profit change in FY25?
reference: Consolidated net profit decreased 11% to INR 72,584 million in FY 2025 from INR 81,725 million in FY 2024.

question: How many passengers did IndiGo carry in FY25?
reference: IndiGo carried 119.77 million passengers in FY 2025, 12.5% more than 106.42 million in FY 2024; since November 2024 it has carried over 10 million passengers every month.

question: What dividend did IndiGo's board recommend for FY25?
reference: A final dividend of INR 10 (100%) per fully paid equity share of INR 10 each, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.

question: What happened to IndiGo's CASK in FY25?
reference: CASK increased 6.4% from Rs. 4.38 in FY 2024 to Rs. 4.66 in FY 2025, mainly due to escalation in maintenance charges, higher airport charges and higher depreciation, partly offset by lower fuel prices.

question: How many permanent employees did IndiGo have at the end of FY25?
reference: 41,049 permanent employees as on March 31, 2025.

question: What was IndiGo's total cash at the end of FY25?
reference: Total cash increased 38.7% to Rs. 481,705 million as of March 31, 2025, with free cash of Rs. 331,531 million and restricted cash of Rs. 150,174 million.

question: What was TCS's revenue in FY24 and its growth rate?
reference: TCS revenue from operations was Rs. 240,893 crore in FY 2024, up 6.8% from Rs. 225,458 crore in FY 2023 (versus 17.6% growth the year before).

question: What was TCS's operating (EBIT) margin in FY24?
reference: EBIT margin was 24.6% in FY 2024 excluding a one-time item (24.2% as reported), compared with 24.1% in FY 2023, helped by productivity, utilisation and lower subcontractor costs.

question: What was TCS's net profit attributable to shareholders in FY24?
reference: Profit after tax attributable to shareholders was Rs. 45,908 crore as reported (Rs. 46,585 crore excluding a one-time item), up from Rs. 42,147 crore in FY 2023.

question: What dividend and buyback did TCS return to shareholders for FY24?
reference: A final dividend of Rs. 28 per share took the total dividend for the year to Rs. 73 per share, and TCS completed its fifth buyback returning Rs. 17,000 crore.

question: How many employees did TCS have in FY24 and what was its attrition?
reference: TCS had 601,546 employees, with LTM attrition in IT services of 12.5%, down 760 bps over the previous year.

question: What was TCS's total contract value (TCV) of deal wins in FY24?
reference: TCV of deal wins was US$ 42.7 billion, double-digit growth.

question: What share of TCS's workforce were women in FY24?
reference: Women made up 35.6% of the employee base, and the workforce spanned over 152 nationalities.

question: Why was TCS's revenue growth muted in FY24 despite record deal wins?
reference: New deals converted into revenue as expected, but those inflows were offset by reductions in the existing revenue base as earlier projects were completed, optimised or downsized, amid macro uncertainty and geopolitical volatility.

question: What were Infosys's revenues in fiscal 2024 and how much did they grow?
reference: Revenues were $18,562 million in fiscal 2024, up $350 million or 1.9% from $18,212 million in fiscal 2023.

question: What was Infosys's net profit in fiscal 2024?
reference: Net profit was $3,169 million in fiscal 2024.

question: How many employees did Infosys have as of March 31, 2024?
reference: Infosys had 317,240 employees as of March 31, 2024, up from 242,371 in 2020.

question: What share of Infosys's fiscal 2024 revenue came from fixed-price contracts?
reference: About 53% in fiscal 2024 (52% in fiscal 2023); products and platforms were 5.5% of revenue.

question: What were Infosys's revenues in fiscal 2025 and the growth in reported and constant currency?
reference: Revenues were $19,277 million in fiscal 2025, growth of 3.9% in reported currency (from $18,562 million) and 4.2% in constant currency.

question: How many employees did Infosys have as of March 31, 2025?
reference: 323,578 employees as of March 31, 2025.

question: Who were Infosys's chairman and CEO according to its fiscal 2025 annual report?
reference: Nandan Nilekani was the non-executive, non-independent Chairman and Salil Parekh the Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director.

question: What share of Infosys's fiscal 2025 revenues was denominated in US dollars?
reference: 64.2% of revenues in fiscal 2025 were in US dollars, down from 66.2% in fiscal 2024 (the euro share rose to 16.8% from 14.8%).

question: Compare the revenue growth of InterGlobe Aviation and Infosys in FY24.
reference: IndiGo's revenue from operations grew about 26.6% (Rs. 544,465 million to Rs. 689,043 million) while Infosys's revenues grew 1.9% ($18,212 million to $18,562 million), so IndiGo grew far faster.

question: Compare the revenue growth of IndiGo and TCS in FY24.
reference: IndiGo grew revenue about 26.6% to Rs. 689,043 million, while TCS grew 6.8% to Rs. 240,893 crore.

question: How did IndiGo's revenue growth in FY25 compare with FY24?
reference: Growth slowed from about 26.6% in FY 2024 (to Rs. 689,043 million) to about 17.3% in FY 2025 (to Rs. 808,029 million).

question: In FY25, did IndiGo's profit move in the same direction as its revenue?
reference: No. Revenue grew about 17% to INR 808,029 million but net profit fell 11% to INR 72,584 million from INR 81,725 million.

question: How did Infosys's revenue growth in fiscal 2025 compare with fiscal 2024?
reference: Growth improved from 1.9% in fiscal 2024 ($18,562 million) to 3.9% in fiscal 2025 ($19,277 million).

question: Compare the employee headcount of TCS, Infosys and IndiGo at the end of FY24.
reference: TCS had 601,546 employees, Infosys 317,240 and IndiGo 36,860 permanent employees, so TCS was almost twice Infosys and about 16 times IndiGo.

question: Compare the FY24 dividends of IndiGo and TCS.
reference: IndiGo did not recommend any dividend for FY 2024 because of losses carried forward, while TCS paid a total dividend of Rs. 73 per share (including a Rs. 28 final dividend) plus a Rs. 17,000 crore buyback.

question: How did Infosys's headcount change between March 2024 and March 2025?
reference: It rose from 317,240 to 323,578 employees, an increase of 6,338 (about 2%).
